text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- President Farooq Leghari and his Kazakhstan counterpart Nursultan Nazarbayev called for Kabul to be cleared of weapons and ammunition ahead of peace talks led by the United Nations.
- All opposition parties led by the Pakistan Muslim Leaque met to discuss options against the government including mass resignation from the legislative assemblies.
- The rupee breached the 43-rupee barrier in the kerb market and was last quoted at 43.10 against the dollar on strong speculative buying triggered by rumours of further devaluation.
- The visiting five-member team of the International Monetary Fund met the new Finance Minister Naveed Qamar.
- Banks may not get the 17 percent annual return on special forex deposits between October 22 and November 28 offered by the central bank if the same amount is withdrawn during this period.
- The Bangladesh Shipping Corporation imposed a $5.0 per tonne congestion surcharge on Port Qasim, claiming substantial losses due to long delays in berthing its vessels.
- The state-run Export Promotion Bureau plans to send a delegation of Pakistani exporters to Iraq for the Baghdad International Fair on November 1 to 15.

- The new macroeconomic package provides a good basis for the resumption of the stalled standby facility of the IMF and it is expected that the Fund will approve the release of $160 million by the end of November.
- Foreign banks are ready to bring in over $175 million by November 28 to benefit from high-yield special deposits and concessions announced by the central bank on October 22.

- Jamaat-i-Islami leader Qazi Hussain Ahmed urged President Farooq Leghari to send Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto's government packing because they are "corrupt, incompetent and do not meet the constitutional requirement of Article 62".
- Refuting rumours that the armed forces wanted to undo democracy in Pakistan, Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto said they were totall impartial.
- Opposition parties decide to hold rally in Rawalpindi on November 12 to get the people's "final decision" against the government.
